sections.h2: Warner Ranch is in Tempe, and we work there
sections.body:
People often group Warner Ranch with Chandler because it sits along the shared border, but the community is in the City of Tempe, ZIP 85284. Its sub-parcels, including Warner Ranch Estates, Warner Ranch Village and Warner Ranch Crossing, all carry Tempe addresses.

Tempe is part of our regular service area. Our crews drive in from our Gilbert office for repairs, inspections and full re-roofs, so the city line makes no difference to how we schedule your job.

sections.h2: What 30-plus years does to a tile roof
sections.body:
Concrete tile itself can last a very long time, but the felt underlayment beneath it is the part that keeps water out, and in Arizona heat felt often lasts around 20–25 years. Homes built in Warner Ranch between 1986 and 1994 are now well past that window if they still have their original underlayment.

Aging felt turns brittle, cracks at the laps and starts to tear around vents and valleys. From the street the roof can look fine while the layer underneath has stopped doing its job.
bullets: Water stains on ceilings near exterior walls or around vent pipes
Slipped or cracked tiles that expose the underlayment to sun
Granules or felt fragments collecting in gutters and at downspouts
Attic sheathing that looks dark or soft after a monsoon storm

sections.h2: Re-felt or full replacement?
sections.body:
For many Warner Ranch homes the answer is a tile underlayment replacement, sometimes called a re-felt or lift and relay. We remove the tile, replace the underlayment and flashings, then reinstall the good tiles and swap in matching ones for any that are broken.

A full roof replacement makes more sense when the decking is damaged, when too many tiles are broken to match, or when an owner wants a new look. We explain both options during the estimate and let you decide.

sections.h2: Foam and flat sections on some Warner Ranch homes
sections.body:
At least one Warner Ranch Village listing shows a home with both tile and foam roofing. Low-slope areas over patios, additions or rear rooms are common on homes of this era, and they age differently from the tile.

Spray foam needs a fresh protective coating every several years to block UV. If the coating wears through, the foam underneath starts to erode. We handle foam roof recoats and flat roof repairs alongside tile work, so one visit can cover the whole house.

sections.h2: Monsoon season in south Tempe
sections.body:
Monsoon season runs June 15–September 30, and its wind gusts are hard on older tile. A tile that was already loose can lift, slide or break, and wind-driven rain finds any gap in tired underlayment.

After a strong storm, walk the yard and look for broken tile pieces, then check ceilings for new stains over the next few days. If you see damage, our storm damage repair team can document it and make repairs.

sections.h2: Working with the Warner Ranch HOA
sections.body:
Warner Ranch is an HOA community with several sub-parcels, and most Arizona associations ask owners to get architectural approval before changing roof color or material. We don't have the association's specific roof rules on file, so check your CC&Rs or ask the management company before a replacement.

A like-for-like re-felt that reuses your existing tile usually changes nothing visible, which tends to make approval simple. We can provide product details for your application.

Look for broken tile on the ground, tiles that have shifted out of line, and new ceiling stains. Gutters full of debris are another sign the roof took a hit.

sections.h2: Why late-1990s tile roofs need attention now

Concrete tile sheds most of the rain, but the felt underlayment below it does the real waterproofing. In the Phoenix area, that felt commonly lasts about 20–25 years before heat makes it brittle.

Ashley Park homes finished in 1997–1999 have crossed that line. Many owners won't see a problem until a heavy storm pushes water through, so a planned inspection now usually costs less than an emergency repair later.

Ridge and hip tiles, checking that mortar or fasteners still hold
Broken, slipped or missing field tiles
Felt exposed at eaves and edges, where sun damage shows first
Attic signs such as stains, daylight or damp insulation

sections.h2: Repair now or plan a re-felt
sections.body:
If the underlayment is still sound in most areas, a targeted roof repair can fix a leak and buy time. We replace broken tiles, reseal flashings and patch the affected section.

When the felt is failing across the roof, a full tile underlayment replacement is the longer-lasting fix. We remove the tile, install new underlayment and flashing, and reset the tile. Because the look of the roof doesn't change, it fits well in an established HOA neighborhood like this one.

Ashley Park's location near Downtown Chandler and the Loop 202 is convenient, but it doesn't shield homes from monsoon weather. From June 15 to September 30, gusty storms can lift loose tile and drive rain sideways under it.

Trees on mature lots also drop leaves and branches into valleys, which can hold water against the underlayment. Clearing valleys and gutters before monsoon season is an easy way to lower the risk.

sections.h2: Attic heat and ventilation
sections.body:
Underlayment wears out faster when the attic below it runs hot. Blocked soffit vents, crushed insulation baffles or too few roof vents trap heat under the deck, and that heat bakes the felt from underneath while the sun bakes it from above.

During an inspection we look at how your attic breathes. Simple fixes, such as clearing vents or adding ventilation during a re-felt, can help the new underlayment last longer and may make upstairs rooms a little more comfortable in summer.

For now, most tile roofs need inspection and targeted repairs. As they age, a tile underlayment replacement will reuse your existing tile and replace the felt beneath.

sections.h2: Gate and access on private streets
sections.body:
Whitewing at Krueger is gated with private streets. One listing gives directions south on Gilbert Road, west on E Locust Drive, then onto S Neuman Drive. When you schedule, let us know how visitors are cleared.

Large lots usually make it easier to stage materials, but we'll confirm where you'd like trucks and equipment placed so driveways and landscaping stay protected.

sections.h2: Monsoon season on a mixed roof
sections.body:
Monsoon storms between June 15 and September 30 bring wind and heavy rain. On mixed roofs, the transition between tile and flat sections is where water most often gets in.

After a storm, check flat sections for standing water or debris and look for slipped tiles on pitched areas. Our storm damage repair team handles all three roof types.

faqs: What roof types are in Whitewing at Krueger?
Because homes are custom built, roofs vary. Listings show foam roofs, tile roofs and rolled or hot-mop flat sections, sometimes on the same house.
How often should a foam roof be recoated?
Typically every several years, depending on the coating and sun exposure. An inspection shows how much coating remains.
Can you work on both the tile and flat sections at once?
Yes. We handle tile, foam and flat roofs, so one inspection and estimate can cover your whole home.
When were homes in Whitewing at Krueger built?
MLS sample homes date to about 2006–2014.
Can a foam section be coated instead of replaced?
Often, yes. If the foam underneath is still solid and dry, a new coating restores its UV protection. Replacement is needed only when the foam is saturated or badly eroded.
Is Whitewing at Krueger gated?
Yes. It's gated with private streets. Share your visitor process when you schedule.
Where do leaks usually start on a mixed roof?
Often at the transitions between pitched tile and flat sections, around drains and scuppers, and at flashings where the roof meets a wall.
Does the Whitewing at Krueger HOA review roof work?
We don't have the HOA's specific rules. Most Arizona associations review changes to roof color or material, so check with yours first.
What does roof work cost on a custom home?
Custom roofs vary a lot. See our Roofing Cost Guide, and we'll give a written estimate after inspecting. Financing is available.
How do I reach you about a Whitewing at Krueger roof?
The number is 602-548-3770, and we pick up Monday through Friday between 7 am and 5 pm. If we don't answer, leave a message and we'll return your call within 24 hours.

sections.h2: Waterfront living, Arizona roofs
sections.body:
Pinelake Estates is marketed for its waterfront homes on community lakes, with walking paths and a playground. Listing directions go east on Chandler Heights Road, then north on Pinelake Way. Streets include E Crescent Pl, E Tonto Pl, S Nevada St and E Coconino Pl.

Lakes don't change how the sun treats a roof. Homes here face the same heat, UV and monsoon storms as the rest of Chandler, and their tile roofs age on the same timeline.

sections.h2: Where 20–23 year old roofs stand
sections.body:
Trend Homes built Pinelake Estates from 2003 to 2005. Felt underlayment under concrete tile commonly lasts 20–25 years in Arizona, so these roofs are now in that range.

Some will hold up for a few more years; others are already letting water through in heavy rain. The only way to know is to look under the tile, which is what our roof inspections do.

sections.h2: Five floor plans, different roof lines
sections.body:
Pinelake Estates was built with five model plans: Sonata, Harmony, Melody, Portales and Prelude. Different plans mean different roof shapes, and roofs with more valleys, hips and wall transitions have more places for water to find a way in.

If neighbors with the same plan have had leaks in a specific spot, it's worth checking that area on your own roof too.

sections.h2: Condos and basements
sections.body:
Pinelake Estates includes some condo units on S Pinelake Way. If you own a condo, check whether your association handles the roof before scheduling work. Responsibility varies.

Some homes here also have basements, which is unusual in Arizona. A roof leak that travels down an interior wall can reach a lower level, so it's especially important to catch problems early in homes with basements.

sections.h2: Your options
bullets: Targeted repair: replace broken tiles, reseal flashings and fix a local leak
Tile underlayment replacement: lift the tile, install new felt and flashings, reset your tile
Full replacement: new tile and underlayment when the deck or tile can't be saved
Storm repair: document and fix monsoon damage
sections.body: We'll recommend the option that fits your roof's condition. Learn more about tile roofs, repairs and roof replacement.

sections.h2: Signs to watch for between inspections
sections.body: You don't need to climb on the roof to spot trouble. Most early warnings show up inside the house or from the yard.
bullets: Ceiling stains or bubbling paint, especially on the top floor
Damp spots or a musty smell in a basement after heavy rain
Cracked or slipped tiles visible from the walking paths or street
Dark felt showing along the lower edge of the roof
Gutters overflowing at the same corner every storm

sections.h2: Monsoon and HOA notes
sections.body:
Each year, monsoon season covers June 15–September 30. After a storm, look for broken tile and new ceiling stains, and call our storm damage repair team if you find any.

We don't have the Pinelake Estates HOA's roofing rules. Most Arizona HOAs review changes to roof color or material, so check before choosing new tile.
